audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer-funded operating float rather than distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.662 billion bridge addition, equal to $23.23 per share; filed June 30, 2026 loyalty deferred revenue was $3.530 billion and air traffic liability was $2.398 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all unrestricted cash and short-term investments to equity value; any amount required to fund ticket, loyalty, liquidity, or other operating obligations is not excess cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, Atmos Rewards program had approximately 480 billion points outstanding, resulting in a deferred revenue balance of $2.9 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that the entire $2.662 billion is unavailable, so this is an unresolved classification issue rather than a proved $2.662 billion error. Its scale is nevertheless material: the cash addition exceeds the absolute equity value in the bear and base cases and represents $23.23 per share.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash and investments to ticket and loyalty proceeds, restricted or pledged balances, covenant liquidity, seasonal working capital, and minimum operating cash; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash and confirm that redemption and ticket-service cash costs enter OE once.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be credited without the aircraft reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.388 billion of filed aircraft purchase commitments at June 30, 2026, versus operating PVs of $3.921-$5.780 billion; 2026 planned capital expenditures were $1.4-$1.5 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: Aircraft spending required for forecast capacity growth must reduce OE through growth investment or, if financed, through incremental interest and other financing costs retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, Alaska had firm orders to purchase 174 B737 aircraft, with deliveries expected between 2026 and 2035, and firm orders to purchase 12 B787 aircraft with deliveries expected between 2026 and 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the investment program is very large, but it does not allocate the commitments between replacement and expansion or establish what the maintenance-capex deduction already captures. The potential omission is reasonably capable of materially overstating operating value because the commitments exceed every scenario's operating PV.
audit_findings.action: Build an aircraft-by-aircraft replacement-versus-expansion schedule, reconcile replacement spending to maintenance capex, assign expansion spending or resulting financing costs to each growth scenario, and rerun OE without double counting leased or CPA aircraft.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may perpetuate acquisition costs that are not terminal expenses
audit_findings.magnitude: $193 million of filed 2025 integration costs and $250 million of total operating special items; these equal 52.4% and 67.9%, respectively, of the $368.4 million absolute OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Finite merger and integration costs embedded in the negative 2025 OE anchor are compounded through the explicit forecast and terminal value as though they recur indefinitely.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the Company incurred costs directly attributable to the merger activities of $ 193 million .
audit_findings.explanation: Embedding the costs is demonstrated if the reported special items entered OE without normalization. Whether all $250 million should be removed is unresolved because some cash costs may recur or continue during integration. The $193 million merger component alone is more than half the absolute anchor, making the issue capable of changing the sign and shape of scenario values even though 2026 still includes integration spending.
audit_findings.action: Trace each component of the $250 million into OE, determine its after-tax cash effect, retain recurring items, separately schedule remaining finite integration outlays—including the $77 million reported for first-half 2026—and rerun all scenarios with a normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ruling ignores the Hawaiian acquisition break
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2024 pro-forma revenue was $13.779 billion versus $11.735 billion reported, a $2.044 billion difference; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the business represented by historical OE, RONTA, volatility, and growth evidence, while current OE and shares represent the combined company.
audit_findings.evidence: As Hawaiian Holdings, Inc. was acquired by Air Group on September 18, 2024, its financial results were not reflected in reported figures in the periods preceding the acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: Hawaiian's pre-September 18, 2024 results are absent from reported history, so legacy, partial-combination, and full-combination years are not comparable. The direction cannot be inferred from revenue or net income alone because owner earnings also depends on reinvestment and cash adjustments, but the $2.044 billion revenue discontinuity is large enough to invalidate the null-perimeter treatment materially.
audit_findings.action: Mark September 18, 2024 as an explicit perimeter break, rebuild 2023-2024 combined OE from filed pro-forma information and underlying cash items where available, and rerun the too-hard assessment, RONTA, and growth cases on a consistent combined-company basis.

audit_findings.title: Committed but uncommenced leases are absent from both the anchor and stated lease context
audit_findings.magnitude: $342 million expected lease liability, equivalent to $2.98 per share if treated as a direct bridge amount and 13.6% of the absolute base-case equity value; actual OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Fixed payments beginning in 2026-2027 can reduce forecast OE, and the associated liability should also be reflected in lease context without duplicating CPA expense, capex, or existing lease charges.
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities expected with these leases are expected to be approximately $ 342 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The future leases and estimated liability are filed facts, but $342 million is a lease-liability estimate rather than an incremental expense or a standalone equity deduction. The record lacks payment timing, operating benefits, and overlap with modeled costs, so it cannot establish the valuation effect; the scale is too large to classify as immaterial without that reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the commencement dates and fixed-payment schedules, identify related capacity or service benefits, reconcile them to CPA expense, capex, and existing lease costs, then rerun forecast OE and update lease context without deducting the same economics twice.

audit_findings.title: Pension cash funding can exceed the expense retained in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $71 million of estimated 2026 required contributions versus $22 million of 2025 qualified-plan pension expense, a $49 million gap equal to 13.3% of the absolute OE anchor and $0.43 per share for one year; qualified plans were $33 million underfunded at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE retains accounting pension expense instead of normalized cash funding while the bridge makes no adjustment for uncovered benefit obligations, cash costs owed ahead of common equity can be understated.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to have approximately $ 71 million in estimated required contributions for its plans in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The one-year cash-versus-expense mismatch is demonstrated, but it is not established that the $49 million difference is recurring or omitted from the OE calculation. Required contributions can reflect funding timing rather than current economic cost, and deducting both normalized contributions and the associated deficit would double count. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE calculation to actual pension contributions, service cost, interest, expected asset returns, funded status, and post-retirement obligations; determine normalized cash funding and rerun OE using either that funding measure or a bridge deduction for the uncovered liability, but not both.
